title: Introduce codelab: embedded RAG playbook with live assertions and compact runner
author: Marta Chen
release_notes: Adds an interactive codelab asset to redwood-examples: an embeddable RAG playbook with a compact live-runner, stepwise assertions, and telemetry presets for debugging streaming and tool-calling flows.
description: Context: engineers asked for a short, runnable codelab that demonstrates building a RAG-driven agent with tool-calling, structured-output contracts, and step assertions that surface regressions quickly during authoring. Motivation: existing examples focus on full apps or CLI runners; this change adds an embeddable browser-first lab that can be dropped into docs site pages and executed locally via a small Go/TS runner. What this PR does: 1) adds codelabs/rag-embedded-lab with a guided README, minimal index.html playground, a compact Go runner that launches a local debug proxy and wasm shim, a TypeScript wasm shim for in-browser tool stubs, and a JSON-based assertion harness for stepwise checks; 2) integrates a lightweight telemetry probe preset (span/event hooks) so authors can see per-step latency and model fallback traces; 3) extends docs/codelabs.md with instructions and a short troubleshooting section; 4) includes sample prompts and a small seeded corpus for deterministic smoke tests. Checklist: - [x] Add README and guided step checklist - [x] Implement compact runner and wasm shim - [x] Add assertion examples and structured-output contract linting hook - [x] Add telemetry presets and doc snippets - [x] Add CI smoke test for runner (headless) - [x] Add short security notes (CORS/auth) Usage notes: the codelab is designed to be dropped into the docs site as an iframe or embedded snippet; it runs against the local runner that proxies to Redwood dev credentials (instructions in README). The assertion harness can be run independently to validate prompt variants and catch regressions during model rollouts. Security and privacy: runner defaults to read-only test dataset and requires explicit env vars for API keys; docs include KMS/HSM notes for Private installs. Backwards compatibility: no changes to runtime or API surfaces; purely examples and tooling. Related: references ENG-1298 for telemetry presets and PM-472 for codelab curriculum. Merge notes: squash-merged after final signoff.

feat(wasm): add TS wasm shim for in-browser tool stubs

docs: update docs/codelabs.md and troubleshooting section
chore: telemetry probes preset and sample spans
review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice focused surface area. Can we keep the runner dependency footprint minimal? Prefer stdlib-only Go where possible.
Marta Chen: Reworked runner to remove 3rd-party HTTP mux; using net/http only. Also added env var gating for debug endpoints.
Lena Ortiz: Request: add a short troubleshooting note about CORS when embedding the iframe and an explicit warning for production keys.
Marta Chen: Added troubleshooting section and explicit warning; default runner now refuses production keys unless FORCE_RUNNER_PROD is set.
Harper Singh: Telemetry probe looks good; one nit on span naming to match the tracing schema (use 'codelab.step' instead of 'step'). Updated before merge.
Harper Singh: Approved and confirmed CI smoke run succeeded locally.
notes: This codelab is intentionally compact: the goal is a low-friction teaching asset with minimal infra assumptions. The assertion harness uses a simple expect/contains model to make step checks readable in CI. Future follow-ups: add TypeScript client bindings for the assertion runner and a docsite plugin to auto-embed runnable previews.
examples_quickstart_snippet: 1) git clone; 2) cd codelabs/rag-embedded-lab; 3) make run-local; 4) open http://localhost:8080 in browser; 5) click 'Run Step 1' to see assertion and trace
